description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved classic in Indian cuisine, known for its lusciously creamy and mildly spiced tomato-based gravy. Tender pieces of marinated chicken are simmered in this rich sauce, creating a dish that is both comforting and incredibly flavorful. Perfect for a hearty family meal, it promises a delightful culinary experience.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in hot water for 15 min

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1/2 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric, 1/2 tsp garam masala, lemon juice, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours for deeper flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until lightly browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, remaining ginger-garlic paste, green cardamoms, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Saute until onions are soft and translucent, about 8-10 minutes.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Add the crushed tomatoes, remaining 1/2 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, and 1/2 tsp garam masala to the pan. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the oil separates. Stir in the soaked cashews.

instructions.title: Blend the Gravy
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamoms (if desired, or blend them). Carefully transfer the gravy mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. If needed, add a splash of water to achieve desired consistency. Strain the gravy back into the pan for an extra silky texture, pressing solids through a sieve.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the smooth gravy to the pan over low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces, sugar, and crushed Kasoori Methi. Stir gently and simmer for another 5-7 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. Stir in the heavy cream and the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter until melted and well combined.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve your classic Butter Chicken hot with naan bread, roti, or steamed basmati rice. Enjoy the rich and creamy flavors!

tips: For an extra smoky flavor, char the marinated chicken in a tandoor or under a broiler before adding to the gravy.
Soaking cashews before blending makes the gravy incredibly smooth and adds a rich, nutty depth without overpowering the dish.
Always add cream and butter at the very end of cooking and avoid boiling the gravy vigorously afterwards to prevent separation and maintain its luscious texture.
article:
Butter Chicken, known traditionally as Murgh Makhani, is more than just a dish; it’s a global culinary phenomenon that has captivated palates with its rich, creamy, and subtly spiced profile. Originating from the bustling kitchens of North India, this beloved Indian chicken recipe has transcended borders to become a staple in Indian restaurants and home kitchens worldwide. Its irresistible allure lies in the perfect marriage of tender, succulent chicken pieces swimming in a velvety tomato-based gravy, enriched with butter and cream. If you’ve ever yearned to recreate that authentic, restaurant-quality Butter Chicken experience at home, you’re in the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through the history, ingredients, and step-by-step process to master this classic dish, ensuring a truly unforgettable meal.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?
Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Its origins trace back to the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s. The story goes that the chefs, looking for a way to use leftover tandoori chicken, tossed it into a rich tomato gravy thickened with butter and cream. The result was a revelation – a dish that perfectly balanced the smoky char of the chicken with a luxurious, tangy-sweet sauce.

At its heart, Butter Chicken features marinated chicken, traditionally cooked in a tandoor (clay oven), though pan-frying or grilling works perfectly for home cooks. This chicken is then gently simmered in a luscious gravy made from tomatoes, onions, ginger, garlic, and a delicate blend of spices. The signature richness comes from generous amounts of butter and cream, often enhanced by ground cashews for an extra layer of decadence and thickness. The final touch of kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves) adds an unmistakable aromatic depth, making Murgh Makhani a symphony of flavors and textures.

## Ingredients for Authentic Butter Chicken
Creating the perfect Butter Chicken requires a few key components, each playing a vital role in building its complex flavor profile.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken (thighs or breast), cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color, regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice
*   Salt to taste

For the Makhani Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more for finishing
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1.5 cups canned crushed tomatoes or fresh tomato puree
*   1/4 cup cashews, soaked in warm water for 15 minutes
*   1 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder (for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar (adjust to taste)
*   1/2 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), lightly crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or half-and-half)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Butter Chicken

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure the chicken is thoroughly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, to allow the flavors to penetrate and tenderize the chicken.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat a grill pan, oven broiler, or a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat. Add a little oil and cook the marinated chicken pieces until they are lightly charred and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. Set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 2 tablespoons of butter with 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Build the Gravy:** Add the crushed tomatoes (or puree), soaked cashews, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, and salt. Stir well and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have softened and the oil begins to separate.
5.  **Blend the Gravy:** Remove the pot from heat and let it cool slightly. Carefully transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. For an extra velvety texture, you can strain the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot, pressing down on the solids to extract all the liquid. Discard any fibrous residue.
6.  **Finish the Makhani Gravy:** Return the smooth gravy to the stove over low heat. Stir in the remaining butter, sugar, garam masala, and crushed kasoori methi. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
7.  **Combine and Serve:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the gravy. Pour in the heavy cream and stir gently. Simmer for another 2-3 minutes, just enough to heat the chicken through and allow it to absorb the rich flavors of the gravy. Do not boil vigorously once the cream is added.
8.  Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot. This classic Butter Chicken is ready to delight!

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken
*   **Marination is Key:** Don't rush the marination process. Longer marination (up to 24 hours) results in more tender and flavorful chicken.
*   **Smooth Gravy:** Blending the gravy until absolutely smooth is crucial for that characteristic restaurant-style texture. Straining it afterwards takes it to the next level.
*   **Kasoori Methi:** This ingredient is non-negotiable for authentic Murgh Makhani flavor. Lightly toasting it in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing enhances its aroma significantly.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** Taste and adjust the sugar, salt, and chili powder. Butter Chicken should have a subtle sweetness and tang that balances the richness.
*   **Don't Skimp on Butter and Cream:** While you can modify for health, the classic taste relies on a generous hand with these ingredients. They contribute to the luxurious mouthfeel and flavor.
*   **Smoky Flavor (Optional):** To mimic the tandoor flavor, after cooking the chicken, place a small piece of burning charcoal in a small heat-proof bowl in the pot with the chicken and gravy. Drizzle a teaspoon of ghee over the charcoal and immediately cover the pot for 2-3 minutes to infuse a smoky aroma.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani
Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs beautifully with a variety of accompaniments.
*   **Breads:** Warm, fluffy naan bread (garlic naan or butter naan are perfect for scooping up the rich gravy), or simple roti/chapati.
*   **Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or aromatic jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast to the creamy curry.
*   **Sides:** A cooling raita (yogurt dip with cucumber or mint) can cut through the richness, and a simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, onion, tomato) adds a fresh crunch.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic recipe is sublime, Butter Chicken can be adapted to suit different preferences and dietary needs.
*   **Vegetarian Options:** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables (peas, carrots, potatoes) for a delicious Paneer Makhani or Vegetable Makhani.
*   **Dairy-Free:** Use coconut cream or full-fat coconut milk instead of dairy cream, and vegan butter for a dairy-free version.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder. For more heat, add finely chopped green chilies to the gravy base.
*   **Healthier Twist:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or use Greek yogurt instead of heavy cream for a lighter but still flavorful version.

## Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What gives Butter Chicken its signature red color?
A: The vibrant red color comes primarily from Kashmiri red chili powder, which imparts color without excessive heat, and the rich tomato base.

Q: Can I make Butter Chicken ahead of time?
A: Absolutely! Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld. Store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.

Q: Can I freeze Butter Chicken?
A: Yes, you can freeze it. For best results, freeze the gravy without the cream. Thaw, reheat, and then stir in the fresh cream just before serving. It will keep in the freezer for up to 2-3 months.

Q: Is Butter Chicken spicy?
A: Traditionally, Butter Chicken is mildly spiced with a creamy, sweet, and tangy profile. The heat level can be adjusted to your preference by varying the amount of chili powder.

Mastering the art of Butter Chicken at home is incredibly rewarding. With this detailed guide, you have all the tools to create a truly authentic and unforgettable Murgh Makhani that will impress your family and friends. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to indulge in one of India's most cherished culinary treasures. Enjoy your homemade Butter Chicken!
